faqs.a: AFP recruits must be at least 18 years old, be Australian citizens, hold a valid Australian driver's licence, meet character standards and have at least a Year 10 Certificate. There is no upper age limit, but every recruit must pass health, fitness and security checks before selection.
faqs.q: What are the AFP eligibility requirements in 2026?

faqs.a: Recruits attend 4 to 6 months of paid training at AFP College in Canberra, learning defensive tactics, driving, firearms and investigations, then are sworn in as police officers or protective service officers. NSW Police recruits train through the Associate Degree in Applied Policing at Goulburn.
faqs.q: How long is Australian police training?

faqs.a: NSW Police applicants need Year 12 HSC with a minimum ATAR of 50 or equivalent, such as a Certificate III, diploma or degree, plus English language proficiency. AFP recruits need at least a Year 10 Certificate, making the federal pathway more accessible on education.
faqs.q: What education is needed to join the police in Australia?

faqs.a: AFP recruits must prove they can swim 100 metres freestyle, hold current first aid and CPR certifications, and pass a minimum-level fitness assessment. NSW Police also requires competent swimming. Candidates should train for endurance running, functional strength and the 100m swim well before applying.

headline: Australia Police Recruitment 2026: AFP and NSW Police Requirements Guide
metaDescription: Australia police recruitment 2026: AFP age 18+ and no upper limit, Year 10 minimum, 100m swim test, 4-6 month paid college, NSW Police ADAP pathway explained.

sections.content:
The Australian Federal Police recruits sworn police officers and protective service officers through its new-recruit pathway, with roles now open in Sydney including at the new Western Sydney Airport from 2026. State forces such as the NSW Police recruit separately with their own standards.

The AFP route requires Australian citizenship, age 18 or older with no upper age limit, a Year 10 Certificate or higher, a valid Australian driver's licence and strong character. Recruits get paid while they train, earn qualifications on the job, and gain 30 days of annual leave plus 15.4 percent superannuation.
sections.title: AFP Recruitment Pathway and Benefits

sections.content:
NSW Police applicants must be at least 18, hold Australian citizenship, permanent residency or New Zealand citizenship, and have a current driver's licence with at least six months of driving experience. Academic entry runs through the Associate Degree in Applied Policing at Western Sydney University, requiring Year 12 HSC with ATAR 50 or equivalent qualifications.

NSW also runs a Cadet Traineeship Program for 16 to 21-year-olds, a 12-month paid traineeship completing a Certificate III in Business that fast-tracks competitive applicants toward the full police application.
sections.title: NSW Police: ADAP and Cadet Traineeship

sections.content:
AFP recruits must demonstrate a minimum fitness level, swim 100 metres freestyle, and hold current first aid and CPR certifications before selection. Training at AFP College in Canberra lasts four to six months and covers defensive tactics, driving, firearms, investigations and national security duties.

NSW Police recruits train at the Police Academy in Goulburn through the ADAP, blending online study, face-to-face training and operational placements. Both pathways combine physical readiness with legal knowledge, communication skills and scenario-based judgement training.
sections.title: Fitness Standards and Police College Training

sections.content:
AFP applicants complete an employment suitability questionnaire, security clearance vetting through the Australian Government Security Vetting Agency, mandatory drug testing and fingerprinting. Emotional intelligence and psychological assessments screen for resilience, and retakes of some tests carry a one-year wait.

AFP recruits also need a BMI between 20 and 29.9. Criminal history, traffic, associations and social media checks apply across both federal and state forces, and dishonesty during vetting is disqualifying. Apply only when every eligibility box is already ticked.
